findings.title: The public harness copy recipes are not closed over their imports

evidence.note: Defines the portable diagnostics and hook/control core as explicit file lists.
Tells adopters to copy those listed files as minimal and advanced starters.
The advertised entrypoint imports atomic-write, manifest, path, shim-file, and shim-template modules omitted from the copy list.
The advertised portable generator imports omitted modules, including the Musi lint-ratchet registry classified elsewhere as an adapter.

evidence.measurement: 18 unique relative import targets outside the six-file hook/control list, measured by extracting and sorting relative imports from the six advertised files at the pin
evidence.note: The documented copy set cannot compile or execute without an undocumented dependency closure.

findings.problem: The outsider-facing adoption ladder presents runnable copy sets, but both starters omit required modules and the purported portable generator reaches into Musi policy. An adopter receives a broken checkout with no reliable reusable-versus-adapter boundary.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat the implementation import graph as authoritative. Publish an import-closed portable package/example or generate and check a complete copy manifest; until then, document the full closure and Musi-specific edits.

findings.title: Lint-ratchet adoption docs mix the packaged engine with its retired copy-set architecture

evidence.note: Tier 1 describes a self-contained engine package and adopter-owned adapter, but also incorrectly makes Musi's diagnostics envelope intrinsic to the runner.
The same checklist requires edits to Musi-only registry, diagnostics, sidecar, and portable-test files outside the stated package copy set.
The reference points to the nonexistent scripts/lint-ratchet/ratchet-globs.ts rather than the packaged kernel implementation.
CI advice still links to removed runtimeFiles/expandDirectories instructions.
The package README assigns registry, CLI composition, harness wiring, and envelope rendering to the adopter-owned adapter.
The authoritative package-boundary test asserts that the engine has no imports escaping the package.

findings.problem: External adopters cannot follow one coherent Tier-1 recipe: the guide first describes the landed package seam, then requires edits to files neither copied nor imported by that package.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat package exports, package-boundary tests, and the demo adapter as authoritative. Rewrite Tier 1 around package plus adopter-owned adapter and remove obsolete copy-set, import-rewrite, and manifest vocabulary.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: CQ25-12 records the package seam as landed with no work left; this finding identifies documentation that still teaches the superseded seam.

findings.title: Devcontainer quick start depends on undocumented local infrastructure

evidence.note: The complete quick start only tells a newcomer to copy the env file and open VS Code.
The build starts from localhost/claude-devcontainer:latest, which cannot be pulled and has no build source in this repository.
Podman is told to use a devcontainers.slice cgroup supplied by a separate host setup.
The persist volume is external and must already exist.
The reuse section nevertheless says copying the directory and adjusting environment, services, and ports is sufficient.

findings.problem: A fresh contributor or harness adopter cannot follow the documented quick start from repository contents alone. The same hidden dependencies make the advertised copy-and-reuse workflow inaccurate.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat Dockerfile and Compose as authoritative: make the base reproducible or pullable and auxiliary resources self-provisioning, or place explicit bootstrap prerequisites before Quick start and enumerate every Musi-specific replacement point.

findings.title: The sole in-progress queue is mostly a stale view of completed or deleted work

evidence.note: The repository's only in-progress queue claims landed entries were removed, then lists eleven bounded items including entries it calls resolved and missing source prefixes.
The authoritative source pack says all 55 findings landed, contradicting the queue's open testsuite item.
The authoritative leaf says the design-token work is done while the active queue calls it unimplemented.
The source index says every task is done, contradicting five queue entries.

evidence.measurement: 10 of 11 Open, bounded items are contradicted by source Status headers, explicitly resolved in the queue, or point to missing leaf prefixes; measured against git ls-tree and the first 16 lines of each source index/leaf
evidence.note: Only the mutation-coverage residue was not disproved.

findings.problem: The lifecycle's most prominent active-work signal points backward and forces contributors to re-triage source packs before trusting any item.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat source-pack Status headers as authoritative and retire or regenerate this queue. Add a structural check requiring every in-progress reference to resolve and remain nonterminal.

findings.title: Backlog is simultaneously an action queue, evidence archive, and completed-work store

evidence.note: The governing lifecycle defines backlog as work that still matters and can be promoted into in_progress.
The backlog's own policy calls its contents parked workstreams.
The parked-items list retains a drained pack explicitly as a provenance record.
A retained audit pack says it is closed and all surviving leaves are Done.
Another backlog pack says all findings landed and surviving leaves are historical records.

evidence.measurement: 95 of 297 tracked Markdown files contain Status:...Done within their first 16 lines; measured by enumerating pinned files and scanning header metadata only
evidence.note: This conservative count excludes Closed, Implemented, Superseded, Resolved, and Rejected records.

findings.problem: The directory name no longer predicts whether an item is actionable. Open work, rejected designs, completed leaves, and provenance ledgers share one 301-file namespace.
findings.proposedDirection: Separate actionable backlog from evidence/provenance records, or introduce a generated typed catalog with record class and lifecycle state while retaining history needed for deduplication.

findings.title: The specialist package-script surface has no contributor-facing command catalog

evidence.note: The root manifest exposes 147 scripts in one undifferentiated object.

evidence.measurement: 177 script keys across all 6 tracked package.json files: root 147, demo 8, client 3, server 17, shared 2, lint-ratchet tool 0; measured with jq over each pinned manifest
evidence.note: The total command surface is substantially larger than the everyday subset.
Specialist tooling is documented only by telling contributors to print the raw root script object and consult AGENTS.md.

evidence.measurement: 21 root script keys have zero exact-key mentions in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, README.md, non-agent_notes docs, or tracked README files; measured with fixed-string git grep per key
evidence.note: Examples include code:intel:perf, test:slow, verify:async controls, test:client:split, and harness:hook-timeouts:check.

findings.problem: The raw manifest acts as the command reference but does not communicate purpose, audience, side effects, required cwd, owning guide, or whether a command is a check, repair, generator, CI primitive, or lifecycle hook.
findings.proposedDirection: Add a generated or manifest-backed command catalog grouped by audience and function, carrying package/cwd, purpose, side-effect class, owner documentation, and writer/check relationships.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: CQ25-37 inventories direct children of scripts/ for layout governance; this finding covers the separate user-facing package-command surface.

findings.title: The E2E guide permits raw locators that mandatory lint unconditionally rejects

evidence.note: The selector hierarchy permits a raw CSS locator when no accessible surface exists if a short reason is left.
Canvas/VTT guidance repeats that fallback.
The rule reports every locator call without inspecting a reason or contextual exception.
The rule is enabled as an error for E2E.
The focused test makes raw locator forms invalid, including an aria-label locator.

findings.problem: A contributor following the documented fallback still receives a blocking lint error; prose explaining the locator does not satisfy the enforced rule.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat lint config and focused tests as authoritative. Document the precise reasoned suppression form, or change guide and rule together if raw locators are intended to be impossible.

findings.title: The concurrency rulebook claims three exhaustive patterns, then documents an uncounted fourth mechanism

evidence.note: The opening claims Patterns A/B/C cover every concurrency-sensitive write and tells contributors not to invent a fourth.
The Serializable section says two paths use a shape that Patterns A/B/C cannot express.
The implementation identifies Serializable retry as the commit path and explicitly says none of the three patterns expresses its set-level invariant.

findings.problem: The guide's most prominent taxonomy classifies an established production mechanism as something contributors were told never to invent.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat the detailed Serializable section and implementation as authoritative. Describe three normal row-level patterns plus a narrowly admitted Serializable set-level exception.

findings.title: Architecture documentation promises level-up review and rollback that the product does not expose

evidence.note: Says CharacterLevelChoice records let recent decisions be reviewed and rolled back.
The router exposes levelUp but no review, undo, downgrade, or rollback procedure.

evidence.measurement: 0 production UI consumers of levelChoices; all three pinned-tree client matches are test fixtures or tests, measured with git grep
evidence.note: The persisted rows are not presented as a player-facing review workflow.

findings.problem: A stable architecture document describes a capability rather than current data-model intent, encouraging contributors to design around an assumed reversible workflow.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat the router and current consumers as authoritative. Describe CharacterLevelChoice as an audit/history record today and separate any review/rollback capability into a product decision.

findings.title: Coverage cadence has no retained baseline to compare against

evidence.note: The guide says original baseline notes were deleted, points to purported LOG entries, and defers creating a durable baseline.
The weekly policy nevertheless requires percentage-point comparisons against the absent baseline.

evidence.measurement: 0 tracked coverage-baseline artifacts at the pin; measured from the complete agent_notes filename inventory, while LOG.md has no cited 2026-05-13 or AUD-COV record
evidence.note: There is no durable comparison artifact behind the cadence instructions.

findings.problem: The weekly check can produce coverage but cannot reproducibly apply its own drift thresholds, leaving each operator to invent a comparison point.
findings.proposedDirection: Record a fresh stable baseline and link it here, or explicitly reframe the current command as a one-off floor check until a retained comparison artifact exists.

findings.title: Harness manifest guide undercounts and omits sanctioned direct readers

evidence.note: The guide says exactly two sanctioned readers remain and documents only generate-harness-controls and check-registry.
The authoritative allowlist contains five readers: loader, registration-check, generate-harness-controls, generate-skill-artifacts, and check-registry.

findings.problem: The maintenance guide presents two exceptional shapes as the complete inventory while the enforced map has five entries with materially different roles.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat MANIFEST_DIRECT_READERS as authoritative. Document or generate all five readers grouped by composition seam, typed specialized consumer, and partial-tree/diagnostic exception.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The landed harness cluster changed this surface; the new delta is post-landing prose describing only two of five enforced readers.

findings.title: Two documents both claim to be the authoritative complete harness inventory

evidence.note: Calls ai-harness.md the authoritative single-source inventory of every guide, lint rule, sensor, and gate.
Says its local-rule rows are selected examples and routes the complete catalog elsewhere.
The generated manifest projection independently calls itself the authoritative inventory of every harness control.

findings.problem: Readers cannot determine which inventory is exhaustive. The conceptual map and generated manifest serve different purposes but are both branded as the single authority.
findings.proposedDirection: Make harness.controls.json and its generated projection authoritative for exhaustive membership; describe ai-harness.md as the conceptual architecture, lifecycle, adoption, and gap map.

findings.title: The generated-doc ownership table misclassifies the lint coverage map as wholly hand-maintained

evidence.note: Labels lint-coverage-map.md Hand-maintained and tells contributors to edit the map directly.
Defines hybrid ownership: one marker-delimited table is generated and surrounding policy is hand-maintained.
Forbids hand-editing the generated span and supplies refresh/check commands.
The generator rewrites the marker-delimited block.

findings.problem: The directory-level ownership table can lead contributors to hand-edit bytes owned by a generator.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat the map's marker contract and generator as authoritative. Classify it as Hybrid and list direct-edit versus generation workflows separately.

findings.title: Homebrew module index sends contributors to the wrong registry file

evidence.note: The parent index says shared currently contains only caster-form-utils.ts.
The authoritative child module documents six shared files.
The flow and add-entity recipe say entry-dialog.tsx switches on types and owns registry entries.
The focused child document correctly names entry-editor-registry.ts as the single registry.
The dialog imports the registry API.
The code-authoritative EDITOR_REGISTRY is declared here.

findings.problem: The parent document duplicated child-module details and drifted after the split. Its explicit recipe sends contributors to a registry consumer while hiding most reusable shared helpers.
findings.proposedDirection: Make code and focused child MODULE documents authoritative. Point the parent recipe to entry-editor-registry.ts and replace volatile inventories with child-document links.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The landed client/homebrew work refreshed focused modules; this is remaining parent-index drift at new paths.

findings.title: Server utilities lack an orientation contract despite owning cross-module trust boundaries

evidence.note: The charter requires MODULE docs for large shared folders and surfaces hiding cross-module contracts.

evidence.measurement: 46 direct tracked non-test TypeScript files and no MODULE document at the pin; measured from git ls-tree
evidence.note: This is the largest undocumented application-source directory among the ranked direct-file directories.
One file alone documents the sanctioned write escape, mutation shapes, locks, and writer classes.
The directory owns restricted-delegate trust boundaries.
The same flat directory owns authorization semantics tied to ADR-0002.

findings.problem: The flat directory mixes authorization, race-sensitive mutation capabilities, Prisma typing, mapping, logging, socket access, and domain helpers. Its ownership map is scattered through long comments and remote service docs.
findings.proposedDirection: Add a focused utils/MODULE.md mapping utility families and trust boundaries, naming sanctioned mutation/auth entry points and linking to CONCURRENCY and authorization docs.

findings.title: Major harness implementation directories have only one-line remote descriptions

evidence.note: The charter calls for local orientation on large, subtle, cross-contract surfaces.

evidence.measurement: 42 direct tracked non-test TypeScript files and no MODULE document at the pin
evidence.note: The directory owns manifest validation, generated surfaces, hook wiring, verification projection, diagnostics, and registration checks.

evidence.measurement: 36 direct tracked non-test TypeScript files and no MODULE document at the pin
evidence.note: The directory contains CLI, daemon, protocol, graph, project-cache, and query layers.
The only common orientation is a one-line ownership row per directory.

findings.problem: Two high-churn harness families meet the repository's own MODULE threshold but lack local orientation, forcing contributors to reconstruct authority, state ownership, and internal layering from filenames.
findings.proposedDirection: Add separate local MODULE documents for scripts/harness and scripts/code-intel, identifying facades, clusters, generated/state ownership, and authoritative checks.

priorPackOverlap.novelty: The landed harness cluster added path-policy documentation and changed these internals, but both owner directories remain undocumented locally.

findings.title: Per-worktree guide omits its mandatory devcontainer credential prerequisite

evidence.note: The guide presents automatic secondary-worktree provisioning without a prerequisites section.
worktree:init and worktree:new are described as self-contained provisioning commands.
The authoritative implementation requires the primary checkout's .devcontainer/.env and reads DATABASE_URL only from it.
The separate root setup tells users to create a root .env, which does not satisfy this lookup.

findings.problem: A contributor following the documented root environment setup can create .env successfully and still have worktree provisioning fail because the distinct devcontainer env file is absent.
findings.proposedDirection: Document .devcontainer/.env and a reachable database as explicit prerequisites, link the devcontainer setup, and explain the root .env distinction. The shell implementation is authoritative.

findings.title: Primary onboarding omits the Bash/Unix runtime required by its first development command

evidence.note: Prerequisites list only Bun and Docker, without a supported host OS, Bash, WSL, or devcontainer requirement.
The primary setup path ends with bun run dev.
The dev command is implemented as bash scripts/dev.sh.

findings.problem: The README appears platform-neutral, but its first application command and most quality/worktree commands require Bash. Windows contributors receive no supported WSL, Git Bash, or devcontainer path.
findings.proposedDirection: Declare supported host environments and the Bash requirement in Prerequisites, with a concise Windows path such as WSL2 or the documented devcontainer workflow.

findings.title: Scripts README gives a non-root recovery command that is still relative to the current directory

evidence.note: After explaining nearest-package failures, the guide suggests bun run scripts/harness-check.ts directly, which is also relative to the nested cwd.
Repository-wide guidance supplies the canonical root-anchored --cwd form.
A representative nearest package manifest has no harness:check fallback.

findings.problem: The troubleshooting paragraph diagnoses the cwd problem correctly, then offers an alternative that fails for the same reason.
findings.proposedDirection: Replace the relative direct-entrypoint advice with the root-anchored --cwd form from AGENTS.md and keep one canonical snippet.

findings.title: Two database-writing SRD backfill commands are exposed without an operator runbook

evidence.note: The server manifest exposes backfill:spell-combat and backfill:monster-actions beside routine generation commands.
The spell command performs Prisma updateMany writes.
The monster command overwrites four persisted action fields.
The shared runner connects to serverEnv.databaseUrl and immediately executes the backfill.
The SRD guide documents all four neighboring generate commands but neither backfill.

evidence.measurement: 0 live-documentation references to either backfill script key, measured with fixed-string git grep across onboarding and non-agent_notes documentation
evidence.note: No documentation states environment selection, lifecycle, affected data, rerun expectations, validation, or rollback.

findings.problem: A contributor can invoke database-writing commands from the manifest without documentation explaining which database to target, whether the scripts remain needed or rerunnable, and how to validate or recover.
findings.proposedDirection: Treat implementation as authoritative and add both commands to the SRD runbook with lifecycle, target-environment warning, affected fields, rerun expectations, expected report, validation, backup, and rollback guidance.
